validity_notes: S6 complementarity non-identifiable on this substrate: per-task retrieval pool (registry size 3) <= k=5 for every retriever, so both flat and hierarchical return the full registry on all 40 alias-OOD tasks; coverage is structurally 1.0 for all pipelines and hierarchical coverage gain is identically 0.0. The MIXED outcome reflects a substrate limitation (no truncation to expose complementarity), not an observed advantage or disadvantage of hierarchical retrieval.

Hierarchical index degenerated to 63 singleton themes (one per train episode) under the frozen clustering (Jaccard>=0.6, average linkage, full component sets incl. url_segments). The aggregation level contributed no grouping; the selection layer still ran (adaptive k 2-3, entropy/coverage expansion) but retrieved sets coincide with flat top-k sets. Fragmentation is reported as designed; no post-hoc threshold tuning was applied.

Control NC-NO-APPLICABLE interpretation: the frozen spec null_control defines the criterion as 'UNKNOWN (or gated confidence<0.80)' with false_accept<=0.10, where an accept is an un-gated (confidence>=0.80) executable. EMBED-K1 is by construction an ablation with no applicability evaluation ('verbatim bind (no reconstruction)', spec line 13); its no-applicable outputs all carry confidence 0.196-0.231 (<0.80), i.e. gated, so the formal frozen criterion passes for all 7 pipelines. The prereg summary line ('all pipelines UNKNOWN') admits a stricter status-only reading under which this control would fail and the status would be MEASUREMENT_INVALID; formal spec text (higher precedence) was applied and strict-reading diagnostics are recorded in NC-NO-APPLICABLE.observed.

RAG baselines are genuine: TFIDF vectorizer fit on train-registry episodes only; all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedded locally (available; no fallback path used), query documents constructed only from intent + derived_context (url path, header keys, body keys).

Novel[0] alias forms (e.g. X-Api-Key) appear as low-confidence distractor mechanisms inside some train registries (parent fixture property, 0.8 confidence, never the expected template; verbatim test-template leak remains 0/40). This slightly raises the prior that 'novel' surface forms are known to the index and is disclosed rather than hidden.

Reconstruction floor: the parent genuine RULE (choose_adoptions + rewrite_template_multi + reconstruct_resolve, copied verbatim from EXP-FRONTIER-35773143736) rewrites the correct bound from any single retrieved candidate of the correct alias family; with full-registry retrieval, all reconstructed pipelines reach the 40/40 resolution ceiling already established for exact-intent-scan retrieval in the parent. Alias resolution performance here therefore measures retrieval+reconstruction parity, not hierarchical gain.
Economics: CPU-only run, zero hosted LLM calls/tokens, zero BrowserGym navigations (N_live=0 per Director mandate); no new SPA fixtures created; embed encodings cached per unique string.

Determinism: seed 42 (random.seed(42), np.random.RandomState(42)); deterministic argmax for theme assignment ties (first index); run re-executed twice with identical metrics (raw evidence byte-identical between reruns).
unresolved: Whether hierarchical selection yields retrieval complementarity when the pool actually truncates: smallest next test is a registry with >=8-12 mechanisms per task (pool >> k=5), intra-family component overlap among several candidates of the SAME family (so flat top-k can drop the correct family even when it is present), and held-equal intents; coverage-gain then becomes identifiable.

Whether the 63-singleton-theme fragmentation is specific to the Jaccard>=0.6 threshold on this synthetic family structure (edge weights ~0.5 within-task, ~0 across-task) or a general property of template-parsed component sets; a lower threshold was deliberately not tried post-hoc.

Whether 'coverage of the correct component family' is the right complementarity construct at all once reconstruction can adopt from any single candidate of the correct family: an alternative penalizing wasted retrieval (distinct components per candidate, redundancy of returned candidates vs oracle-minimal set) may be more discriminating for retrieval-layer research.

EMBED-K1 status under applicability controls: the ablation has no applicability evaluation by its frozen definition; a decision on whether control strata should exempt no-reconstruction ablations or whether the ablation should carry a guard would change status classification (see NC-NO-APPLICABLE note).
